messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@helios.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — tenor options and downside protection

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward a committed-reserved plan for steady inference workloads. Before we lock tenor, procurement needs:

- A clear view of how pricing bands change if GPU spot/market rates shift (what protections or indexation do you offer?)
- Approval thresholds required on your side for >$2.5M ARR-commits (do discounts need exec sign-off?)
- Operational exposure: how length of commit maps to capacity guarantees, burst options, and fallback model variants.

Attached is a short ask doc with projected consumption (helios_pricing_request.pdf). Can you outline a default offer + a contingency path if market GPU costs rise materially mid-tenor? We have a July 1 internal board review and need a strawman.

Best,
Jordan
Director, Cloud Ops
Helios AI
[Attachment: helios_pricing_request.pdf (pdf)]
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@helios.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — tenor options and downside protection

Jordan — thanks for the clear brief and the usage file. Quick summary/plan below; I copied Marissa (finance) and Karthik (sales ops) to give the approval/impact view.

Short answer: we can offer three structured options that balance price predictability with GPU-market contingency:

1) Fixed-tenor locked price (12 / 24 / 36 months) — simplest for forecasting; discount tiers tied to commit size.
2) Index-linked tenor — price adjusts quarterly against a pre-agreed GPU-cost index with a symmetric cap/floor to bound downside for both sides.
3) Hybrid staircase — initial locked floor for first 9 months, then partial indexation thereafter; includes a capped rebate if market costs fall.

Operational exposure controls we propose:
- Guaranteed baseline throughput (p99 latency SLA) mapped to a pinned pool.
- Burst pool for spikes with queueing priority and documented fallback to a lighter-weight model (compatible with your inference quality targets).
- Quarterly capacity review and ability to shift SKU mix within agreed bounds.

What we need from you to make this concrete for the board: commit band (preferred months), likely monthly token throughput, and whether you need on-prem/VPC isolation. I attached a quick spreadsheet with menu options (proposed_commit_options.xlsx).

Next steps: Marissa / Karthik — can you run a sensitivity for the three options showing net revenue and margin impact if GPU unit costs increase by +15% / +30%? Also flag where we need exec approval for discount levels.

Jordan — planning to send a straw SOW for review by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_commit_options.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — tenor options and downside protection

Avery / Karthik — ran a rapid sensitivity (attached: finance_impact_calc.csv). Highlights:

- Scenario A (Fixed-price, 24m): at +15% GPU cost, gross margin on the deal drops ~7pp; at +30% it drops ~15pp.
- Scenario B (Index-linked, symmetric cap/floor at +/-10%): shields us up to +/-10%, beyond that exposure is shared per index formula — breakeven at ~+18% for our target margin.
- Scenario C (Hybrid staircase): reduces short-term exposure but leaves medium-term risk if spot remains elevated.

Approval notes: any net discount >22% or any fixed-price tenor >24 months requires VP Finance sign-off (David). Anything that embeds an unconditional price floor below our standard list requires Exec (CRO) approval.

Suggested negotiation levers:
- Convert part of the economic give into non-monetary concessions (longer SLA, multi-year reference, prioritized capacity during launch).
- Add an indexed collar (e.g., cap/floor +/-12%) instead of pure fixed — reduces need for exec escalation.

If you want, I can draft the exact approval memo templates (finance + exec) to attach to the SOW.

Marissa
VP, Revenue Finance
[Attachment: finance_impact_calc.csv (csv)]

Jordan — following internal review, here is a pragmatic path we can take that keeps procurement comfortable and limits exec gating.

Offer (strawman):
- 24-month committed pool sized to your projected average monthly tokens. Base discount: 18% at commit band X (see spreadsheet).
- Indexed collar after month 9: quarterly adjustment vs GPU-cost index with a cap/floor of +/-12% to protect both parties.
- If index moves >+18% for two consecutive quarters, we will trigger a review and agree a short-term uplift for new provisioning (limited to next quarter) — we will not retroactively bill past usage.
- Operational guarantees: pinned baseline pool (SLA p99), burst capacity for peak events (throttled after threshold), and fallback to compatible lightweight model for non-blocking jobs.

Approvals: Marissa confirms VP Finance sign-off is not required for this structure; discount and collar are within delegated limits. Anything more aggressive (discount >22% or fixed price >36m) would require escalation per Marissa's note.

Next steps:
1) Jordan — please confirm your preferred commit band (we used your mid-case in the attached SOW draft) and if VPC/on-prem isolation is required.
2) We will share a redline-ready SOW (helios_sow_draft.pdf) and a DocuSign package.
3) If agreed, legal will prepare final terms; timeline to signature typically 7–12 business days unless there are substantive T&Cs.

Attaching the SOW draft for your review. If you want a 30-minute sync to walk through the index formula and operational guardrails I can schedule time tomorrow.

Best regards,
Avery Johnson
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: helios_sow_draft.pdf (pdf)]
